question.text: The requirement that Investment Committee members be responsible for compliance with SEBI (AIF) Regulations under the 2021 amendment does NOT apply to which of the following fund types?

answer.text: All Category I AIFs regardless of investor profile
Only angel funds registered as sub-category of Cat I AIF
Only Category III AIFs with AUM above INR 500 crore
Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors and AIFs where each investor (other than Manager/Sponsor) has committed at least INR 70 crore and furnished a waiver

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.7.3, the requirement that IC members shall be responsible for compliance does NOT apply to (a) Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors and (b) AIFs where each investor (other than Manager, Sponsor, employees/directors) has committed minimum INR 70 crore or equivalent and has furnished a waiver to the AIF. Reference: SEBI Circular dated June 25, 2021. **The Trap:** Option A is too broad — Cat I is not wholesale exempt. Option C invents an AUM threshold. Option D misidentifies angel funds, which do follow the requirement. **Cross-Exam Context:** LVF / INR-70-crore-waiver carve-outs are heavily tested. XIX-A tests the thresholds; XIX-C tests the operational consequence for IC structuring. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** If onboarding sophisticated INR-70-crore+ LPs, collect the IC-waiver at subscription — doing it post-hoc is a documentation nightmare. Keep the waiver template SEBI-format ready.
